microservices.responsibility: Manages shipment (cargo) registration and lifecycle: creating shipments with origin, destination, and delivery deadline; assigning unique tracking identifiers; enforcing origin/destination rules; changing destinations and triggering replanning decisions; associating chosen routes with shipments; and providing the consolidated administrative view grouped by business status (unrouted, routed and in transit, collected). Owns the core cargo domain model and route specification/itinerary assignment.

Computes and provides candidate routes (itineraries) compatible with a shipment's origin, final destination, and delivery deadline using the pathfinder graph traversal capability. Validates route feasibility, returns route legs with loading/unloading points, trips (voyages), and planned dates, and reports when no feasible option exists. Owns voyage and path-finding logic.

Records logistics events (receipt, loading, unloading, customs, pickup) across multiple channels (operational interface, REST integration, and periodic input-file batch processing). Validates events against existing shipments, locations, and trips; rejects and quarantines invalid records for later analysis; retains event history with occurrence and registration timestamps; and publishes valid events to trigger shipment status recalculation. Ensures resilient per-record processing.

Provides shipment monitoring and tracking by tracking identifier: current status, last known location, estimated arrival time, event history distinguishing expected from off-plan events, off-route deviation flags, and geographic visualization of origin/destination/last known location. Recalculates and consolidates delivery/transport status from handling events and keeps monitoring channels aligned with the most recent information.
Manages the catalog of registered logistics locations used across the system, providing controlled lists for shipment origin/destination selection, route computation, and event location validation.
